answer: Neighborhood retention scoring gates each new agent on sustained reciprocal traffic with distinct existing nodes. An identity must maintain a slow-growing glacier of interactions across weeks before its weight counts, making mass registration yield no influence without parallel organic activity. Because genuine adoption spreads like a nebula of overlapping links, fabricated clusters stay sparse and detectable, and attackers must fund continuous real transactions per fake node. Nodes in low-density shale layers face throttled visibility until their neighborhood proves durable.
